card.title: Godot 4.4 dev idle and editor CPU consumption regression

history: The one known cause (Windows delay_usec busy-wait, df3367f) was reverted upstream in 8e1a6ea and the current master delay_usec is Sleep-only, so the snapshot likely lacks the regression. The seed's fix PR #99656 was never merged. Remaining scope is one lever at about 20 lines, not a long-horizon tas

facts.claim: Issue #99593 exists and reports Windows idle/editor CPU use in 4.4-dev5 (15-18% per project) versus 0.1% in 4.3-stable
Issue is closed; cause traced to df3367f / PR #99178, which turned OS_Windows::delay_usec from Sleep into a busy-wait with a 1.2 ms spin threshold
Issue closed by commit 8e1a6ea 'Revert Make delay_usec more precise', touching only platform/windows/os_windows.cpp with 4 additions and 16 deletions
Seed's reference 'merged upstream fix PR #99656' is merged
Current master OS_Windows::delay_usec contains only Sleep calls, so the Windows spin-wait regression is absent at upstream head
The snapshot at head 1b16fd14 still exhibits high CPU use in the scenarios (seed's task framing)

full_card.band: Low: the one known cause is one function, already reverted upstream; no evidence of a larger hidden regression at head.

v1.kill_reason: The one known cause (Windows delay_usec busy-wait, df3367f) was reverted upstream in 8e1a6ea and the current master delay_usec is Sleep-only, so the snapshot likely lacks the regression. The seed's fix PR #99656 was never merged. Remaining scope is one lever at about 20 lines, not a long-horizon task, and the reported symptom is Windows-only and not reproducible in the Linux sandbox.

Band.why: One known lever, already fixed upstream; no evidence a frontier agent would fail, but the scope is essentially nil.

Build.why: Godot headless build is a few hours on 8 cores; under 5 days, but no verified build from the probe.

Fit.why: Windows-specific symptom cannot be reproduced in the gVisor Linux sandbox.

Hor.why: Find-and-revert is short; not a long-horizon task.

Nov.why: Neighbour S-op-054 at 0.371 is in the same repo family; partial overlap.

Real.why: Real issue and commits exist, but the seed's framing (cause, merged PR 99656, snapshot showing the bug) is contradicted or unverified.

Ref.why: Reference is a ~20-line revert already upstream; not a complete or measured implementation.

Seal.why: Harness and hashes can be sealed, but the fix itself is public history, so it must be stripped.

Surf.why: Only a few fixed-frame headless scenarios with a state hash; no broad surface.

spike_plan.kill_if: No CPU gap above noise on Linux, or the snapshot head already matches 4.3 (the reported Windows regression is fixed upstream).
spike_plan.pass_if: A reproducible CPU-time gap of at least 20% between head and 4.3-stable on a fixed-frame headless scenario, with a hotspot traceable to one or more files.
steps: Clone godot at 1b16fd14 in a throwaway container with network; confirm platform/windows/os_windows.cpp delay_usec is Sleep-only (already checked on master).
Build the Godot headless (scons platform=linuxbsd target=template_release headless) on 8 cores and time it.
Run an idle headless project at 60 fps for a fixed frame count and record CPU time per frame.
Compare with the 4.3-stable headless build on the same project to see whether any gap exists on Linux.
Check whether any Linux code path (os_unix.cpp delay_usec, add_frame_delay) shows a hotspot above noise under perf-free timing (time/getrusage).

v1.summary: Seed S-op-055 is killed as K10: the reported Godot 4.4-dev Windows CPU regression (issue #99593) has a single cause that was already reverted upstream in commit 8e1a6ea, and current master shows no busy-wait in delay_usec. The seed's cited merged fix PR #99656 was closed unmerged, and the claim that the snapshot still exhibits high CPU is unverified and likely false.
